role_evidence.claim: CNA is named as a partner alongside Chubb in the US International Development Finance Corporation maritime reinsurance facility created for Gulf marine war risk.
role_evidence.source_name: Insurance Business, Strait of Hormuz crisis: Why the biggest opportunity in marine war insurance lies ahead
role_evidence.source_excerpt: The US International Development Finance Corporation announced a maritime reinsurance facility on March 6, initially at $20 billion and expanded to $40 billion two weeks later, with Chubb as lead underwriter alongside Travelers, Liberty Mutual, Berkshire Hathaway, AIG, Starr and CNA as partners.

business_summary: CNA Financial Corporation (NYSE: CNA) is a US commercial property-casualty insurer majority-owned by Loews Corporation. It sits on the hormuz-maritime chain's war-risk-reinsurance-capacity link. On war-risk-reinsurance-capacity: named partner insurer in the US International Development Finance Corporation maritime war-risk reinsurance facility standing behind the Gulf marine war account.

exposure_summary.narrative: CNA Financial Corporation sits on war-risk-reinsurance-capacity, scored EMERGING (impact 78, crowdedness 55, capture 52): capacity had to be manufactured rather than bought (a sovereign DFC facility and a separate Lloyd's market consortium), and the trade press's own read is that the episode has not been profitable in aggregate so far. Named partner insurer in the US International Development Finance Corporation maritime war-risk reinsurance facility standing behind the Gulf marine war account.
